parents.lead: Short, calm ways to learn together, and trusted advice on online safety, wellbeing and SEND when you need it.
parents.note: Advice cards name their publisher and the country they cover. Made by Matt makes learning resources and tools; it does not give safeguarding, medical or legal advice. For advice about your own child, speak to their school or the services linked here.
parents.promptsTitle: A small activity is a useful start
prompts: Read and talk
Share a few pages, listen to someone read, or talk about a picture. Ask what might happen next; a spoken answer or pointing is fine.
Notice numbers
Use familiar objects to sort, count or compare. Choose one small task and show an example before taking turns.
Make one thing
Draw, write, record or build one idea. Let your child choose how to show it and talk about a part they enjoyed.
Plan the next step
For a more independent learner, agree a manageable goal and a stopping point. Help with the routine, then let them try the task.

schools.promptsTitle: Questions for your next planning or review meeting
prompts: Adapting the task
Open one lesson. Check the instructions, reading demand and response options, then decide what to change for the pupils in front of you.
Regulation & return
Look at how the lesson starts calmly and gives a clear way back to learning after a break. Ask what your team already does that works.
Evidence of progress
Ask how a small step is noticed and recorded against a pupil’s target, and who uses that record next.
Safeguarding & online safety
Check training against the current statutory guidance and how online-safety teaching fits the curriculum.

trusts.lead: Compare teaching, inclusion and practical tools across your schools, with the governance, safeguarding and data guidance trusts work to.
trusts.note: The official guidance here is for England; each card names its publisher and jurisdiction. No trust adoption figures, procurement model, licence or endorsement is implied. Made by Matt materials are teacher-created resources.
prompts: Curriculum across schools
Ask two schools to open the same lesson sequence. Compare what pupils build on and how each school would adapt it.
Inclusion
Look at how adaptations are planned, recorded and checked, and whether the approach would work in your specialist and mainstream settings.
Workload & tools
Try one tool with a colleague. Does it save time without adding a new data burden or a new account?
Assurance
Ask how leaders would know an approach is working, and which edition of the guidance applies on which date.

partners.lead: Try the lessons, creative apps and teaching tools in the area you know best, and check the standards schools expect from anyone working with their pupils.
partners.note: The official guidance here is for England or the UK; each card names its publisher and jurisdiction. No partnership scheme, customer list, licence or commercial arrangement is implied. The page presents public work and the established contact email only.
partners.promptsTitle: Before you work with a school
prompts: Try a complete example
Open a lesson or app in the area you know best and judge it against your own materials.
Accessibility
Check that what you offer can be used with a keyboard, a screen reader and large text, and that colour is never the only cue.
Children’s data
Know what personal data you would collect, why, and how the children’s code and the school’s data-protection duties apply.
Safeguarding
Read the part of the statutory guidance that applies to visitors and contractors, and know which checks the school will ask for.
